Visionary

VIZH-uh-ner-ee -- built on the root for 'to see.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Visionary is having or showing highly original and imaginative ideas about the future.

The architect's visionary designs imagined entire cities built around vertical farms.

Worked Example

Decades before anyone else believed it possible, an engineer sketches plans for a device that lets ordinary people carry a computer, a camera, and a telephone all in one pocket-sized object.

That bold, far-ahead imagination is exactly what visionary describes. Unlike 'practical,' which focuses on the present, visionary looks toward possibilities others haven't yet imagined.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

inventive: Inventive emphasizes hands-on cleverness -- actually building or devising something new that works. Visionary is about the reach of the idea itself: a visionary thinker imagines a changed future, whether or not she ever builds anything.

forward-thinking: Forward-thinking means planning sensibly for what is coming -- updating systems before they break, saving before retirement. Visionary is bolder: it imagines futures other people have not even pictured yet, not just prepares for the expected one.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unimaginative: lacking creativity or original thought

conventional: following accepted standards; ordinary

Where it sits · how bold and large the ideas are — imaginative → visionary → revolutionary

imaginative vs. visionary: Imaginative is a broader word than visionary -- imaginative can describe anyone with a creative idea, while visionary specifically implies bold, large-scale ideas about the future.

revolutionary vs. visionary: Revolutionary goes a step beyond visionary: a visionary plan imagines a bold new future, while a revolutionary one actually overturns how things are done, sweeping the old way aside.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vis-

Root — vis-: to see (from Latin videre, 'to see')

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or result of (Latin -io)

Suffix — -ary

Suffix — -ary: relating to, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin videre meant 'to see': vis- ('to see') + -ion ('act or result of') + -ary ('relating to') -- a visionary is, at its root, someone who 'sees' far into the future, imagining possibilities long before anyone else can picture them.

Use the root in a new word: envision

Use the root in a new word: envision: The mayor asked residents to envision what their neighborhood could look like in twenty years.
